defects.title: The MATLAB version check reads the first product listed by ver
defects.trigger: any call after initCobraToolbox: ver lists M2HTML Toolbox 1.5 first on MATLAB R2025a
defects.observed: matlabVersion(1) = 1.5, firthRegression stays false; logistic fits are not Firth-penalised on R2025a and a perfectly separated reaction is dropped (NaN row) instead of fitted
defects.expected: the MATLAB version (ver('MATLAB')), so R2024b+ uses the Firth regression as the comment says

notes: Quarantined by lead decision (wrong-result). Repro: initCobraToolbox(false); v = ver; v(1)  -> M2HTML Toolbox 1.5, so line 141 compares 1.5 >= 24.2 and Firth regression is never used on R2025a; e.g. data = table(["HM_s1";"HM_s2";"HM_s3";"HM_s4";"HM_s5";"HM_s6"], [2;1;4;3;6;5], 'VariableNames', {'ID','rB'}); metadata = table(["s1";"s2";"s3";"s4";"s5";"s6"], ["a";"a";"b";"a";"b";"b"], 'VariableNames', {'ID','Grp'}); performRegressions(data, metadata, 'Grp ~ Flux')  -> separation warnings, results.NotDefined = {'No results'}; with a stand-in ver reporting 24.2 the Firth fit gives a finite estimate 1.1289. Note: the Firth choice is stated in the code comment (lines 133-134), not in the function header. Earlier characterization (now removed from the test, all passing): linear fits match X\\y with textbook SE/t/p/adjusted R2; CI t-based also for binomial; FDR counts NaN rows of dropped models in m. Lines 109 (dead) and 155-158, 220-221 (fitglme) would need exemptions after the fix. Callers performStatsPersephone, runStatisticsOnModerationAnalysisResults reach it.
confirmed_by: lead (source read: the MATLAB version is read from ver(1), the first listed toolbox, lines 136-141, against the evident intent stated in the comment of lines 133-134: Firth regression above R2024b); severity raised to wrong-result by the lead
